1a8n3y5.q: A probable cause of accidents due to the road structure can be narrow road width
1a8n3y5.why: A narrow road leaves little room to manoeuvre or pass other vehicles, so it is a structural defect that favours accidents.

1213chc.q: A probable cause of accidents due to the road structure can be failure to signal intersections
1213chc.why: Unsignalled intersections surprise drivers and lead to right-of-way mistakes, so this is a road-structure defect.

a1i0ea.q: A probable cause of accidents due to the road structure can be lack of road markings
a1i0ea.why: Without road markings (segnaletica orizzontale) drivers cannot see lanes, edges or crossings, which raises the accident risk.

nnt5sy.q: A probable cause of accidents due to the road structure can be a deformed road surface
nnt5sy.why: A deformed surface with potholes or dips makes vehicles lose stability and control.

1nktowu.q: A probable cause of accidents due to the road structure can be a slippery road surface
1nktowu.why: A slippery surface reduces grip, lengthens braking distances and causes skids.

ggkngs.q: A probable cause of accidents due to the road structure can be unsignalled bottlenecks
ggkngs.why: Unsignalled bottlenecks (strettoie) catch drivers by surprise, leaving no time to adjust speed and path.

rw4kwj.q: A probable cause of accidents due to the road structure can be a road divided into carriageways
rw4kwj.why: Dividing a road into carriageways (carreggiate) separates opposing traffic, so it improves safety instead of causing accidents.

lbk5ba.q: A probable cause of accidents due to the road structure can be a road divided into lanes
lbk5ba.why: Dividing a road into lanes organises traffic and reduces risk, so it is not a structural defect.

1winpwl.q: A probable cause of accidents due to the road structure can be a one-way carriageway
1winpwl.why: A one-way carriageway removes head-on conflicts and improves safety, so it is not a structural cause of accidents.

lpwjwg.q: A probable cause of accidents due to the road structure can be a flat road layout
lpwjwg.why: A flat road is favourable for driving; steep gradients, bends and damaged surfaces are the dangerous features.

58mzez.q: A probable cause of accidents due to the road structure can be the presence of side impact-absorbing barriers (guardrails)
58mzez.why: Guardrails absorb impact and keep vehicles on the road, so they protect people rather than cause accidents.

6sqjbj.q: A probable cause of accidents due to the road structure can be traffic light regulation
6sqjbj.why: Traffic lights control crossing flows at intersections and reduce conflicts, so they improve safety.

13k3oyt.q: A probable cause of accidents due to the road structure can be the absence of dangerous bends
13k3oyt.why: Dangerous bends cause accidents; their absence is not a road defect.

f35xo1.q: When it rains you must reduce your speed
f35xo1.why: Rain reduces grip and visibility, so you must slow down.

b3kl5y.q: When it rains you must keep the windscreen wipers on
b3kl5y.why: Wipers (tergicristalli) keep the windscreen clear of water so you can see.

n3sbtd.q: When it rains you must increase the safety distance
n3sbtd.why: Braking distances are longer on wet roads, so you need a bigger safety distance.

18te7mc.q: When it rains you must prevent the windows from fogging up
18te7mc.why: Fogged windows reduce visibility, so use ventilation and demisting to keep them clear.

1fs65r5.q: When it rains you must steer carefully
1fs65r5.why: On wet roads sudden steering inputs can break grip and cause skids, so steer gently.

hcqfpg.q: When it rains you must drive quickly through puddles to avoid getting stuck
hcqfpg.why: Puddles must be crossed slowly; speed encourages aquaplaning and loss of control.

r0i4qc.q: When it rains you must cover the radiator with the special cover
r0i4qc.why: A radiator cover is used in severe cold, not in rain.

1e7p0fh.q: When it rains you must brake hard
1e7p0fh.why: On wet roads hard braking can lock the wheels and cause a skid; brake gradually instead.

16tc6fz.q: When it rains you must use the hazard warning lights (four flashers) while driving
16tc6fz.why: Hazard lights are for signalling danger or an emergency, not for driving in rain.

kgby64.q: When it rains you must normally drive with the clutch pedal pressed down
kgby64.why: Driving with the clutch pressed down reduces control of the vehicle and must always be avoided.

10gkoce.q: The phenomenon of aquaplaning makes the wheels slide on a layer of water
10gkoce.why: In aquaplaning a film of water separates the tyre from the asphalt, so the wheels slide on the water.

mqv2rc.q: The phenomenon of aquaplaning starts at a lower speed if the tyre is badly worn
mqv2rc.why: A worn tread disperses less water, so aquaplaning starts at a lower speed.

16jiu66.q: The phenomenon of aquaplaning occurs more easily in lighter vehicles
16jiu66.why: A lighter vehicle presses less on the road and is lifted more easily by the water film.

1nroivv.q: The phenomenon of aquaplaning occurs more easily at low speed
1nroivv.why: Aquaplaning is more likely at high speed, because the tread cannot clear the water fast enough.

1aou66.q: The phenomenon of aquaplaning reduces vehicle skidding
1aou66.why: Aquaplaning removes grip and control, so it increases the risk of skidding.

oadvcc.q: The phenomenon of aquaplaning increases on carriageways with a steep lateral slope
oadvcc.why: A steep sideways slope helps water drain away, so it is not what increases aquaplaning.

q2e617.q: The phenomenon of aquaplaning increases grip on the road surface
q2e617.why: Aquaplaning removes grip, because water comes between the tyre and the road.

oeegx2.q: The phenomenon of aquaplaning strengthens the contact between tyres and asphalt
oeegx2.why: In aquaplaning the contact between tyres and asphalt is lost, not strengthened.

19atg54.q: The phenomenon of aquaplaning does not depend on the depth and pattern of the tread
19atg54.why: Tread depth and pattern decide how much water is cleared, so they strongly affect aquaplaning.

uyvfgl.q: On snow-covered roads you must fit snow tyres on all wheels or chains on the driving wheels
uyvfgl.why: On snowy roads you need winter tyres on all wheels or snow chains on the driving wheels.

15ysigh.q: On snow-covered roads you must moderate your speed
15ysigh.why: Grip is reduced on snow, so you must moderate your speed.

j61se1.q: On snow-covered roads you must increase the safety distance
j61se1.why: Braking distances grow a lot on snow, so the safety distance must be increased.

13nfoj3.q: On snow-covered roads you must avoid sudden manoeuvres
13nfoj3.why: Sudden manoeuvres on snow make the tyres lose grip and cause skids.

1nzfcky.q: On snow-covered roads you must avoid sudden acceleration
1nzfcky.why: Sudden acceleration on snow makes the driving wheels spin and you lose control.

1c3l9d4.q: On snow-covered roads you must brake harder
1c3l9d4.why: On snow you brake gently; hard braking locks the wheels and causes a skid.

1fdfz0z.q: On snow-covered roads you must accelerate to the maximum when starting off
1fdfz0z.why: When starting on snow you accelerate gently; full acceleration only makes the wheels spin.

134oxv9.q: On snow-covered roads you must steer sharply to avoid hitting stationary vehicles
134oxv9.why: Sharp steering on snow breaks grip; you must slow down and react gradually.

16d8ksb.q: On snow-covered roads you must brake hard if the vehicle skids
16d8ksb.why: If the vehicle skids you do not brake hard, because the wheels would lock; ease off and keep steering control.

c4ogjd.q: On icy stretches of road it is advisable to drive at a moderate speed
c4ogjd.why: Grip is minimal on ice, so drive at a moderate speed.

xzu28k.q: On icy stretches of road it is advisable to increase the safety distance
xzu28k.why: Stopping distance grows greatly on ice, so you need a larger safety distance.

hydmzp.q: On icy stretches of road it is advisable to keep away from the path of vehicles passing in the opposite direction
hydmzp.why: A vehicle can skid on ice, so keep clear of the path of oncoming vehicles.

ay55kw.q: On icy stretches of road it is advisable to use low gears when going downhill
ay55kw.why: Low gears on a downhill use engine braking and avoid braking that could lock the wheels.

wc170x.q: On icy stretches of road it is advisable to avoid sudden acceleration
wc170x.why: Sudden acceleration on ice makes the driven wheels spin.

13xr3d.q: On icy stretches of road it is advisable to pay extra attention when passing through shaded areas
13xr3d.why: Shaded areas stay icy longer, so they need extra attention.

112ra2u.q: On icy stretches of road it is advisable to engage four-wheel drive, if the vehicle has it
112ra2u.why: Four-wheel drive improves traction on ice, if the vehicle is fitted with it.

1fxhud1.q: On icy stretches of road it is advisable to drive very close to the side barrier
1fxhud1.why: Driving close to the barrier is dangerous, because a skid would send you into it.

dn4kyp.q: On icy stretches of road it is advisable to not use chains, but studded tyres on the front wheels
dn4kyp.why: On ice you use chains on the driving wheels or winter tyres, not studded tyres on the front wheels only.

81kpg5.q: On icy stretches of road it is advisable to brake hard every time you pass another vehicle
81kpg5.why: Hard braking on ice locks the wheels and causes a skid, especially when passing another vehicle.

gtp0s0.q: On icy stretches of road it is advisable to drive with the gearbox in neutral
gtp0s0.why: Driving in neutral removes engine braking and reduces control of the vehicle.

bbgcuc.q: In dense fog it is advisable to let the road markings guide you
bbgcuc.why: In dense fog the road markings help you stay in your lane.

fqlxse.q: In dense fog it is advisable to drive at a speed suited to the visibility
fqlxse.why: In fog your speed must let you stop within the distance you can see.

7uuyfl.q: In dense fog it is advisable to stop, if necessary, off the carriageway
7uuyfl.why: If you must stop, doing so off the carriageway reduces the risk of being hit from behind.

vv1cf1.q: In dense fog it is advisable to use the hazard warning lights (four flashers) if forced to stop on the carriageway
vv1cf1.why: If you must stop on the carriageway, the hazard lights warn approaching drivers.

vcnrgx.q: In dense fog it is advisable to avoid stopping on the carriageway except in cases of force majeure
vcnrgx.why: A stationary vehicle in fog is a serious danger, so stop on the carriageway only if you really have to.

p6k2k.q: In dense fog it is advisable to switch on the fog lights or, failing that, the dipped headlights
p6k2k.why: In fog you use the front fog lights or, if you have none, the dipped headlights.

1wy5bj5.q: In dense fog it is advisable to switch on the rear fog light
1wy5bj5.why: In dense fog the rear fog light makes your vehicle visible to drivers behind from far away.

1cefdbm.q: In dense fog it is advisable to drive with maximum care and concentration
1cefdbm.why: Visibility is reduced in fog, so you need maximum care and concentration.

14dyf2j.q: In dense fog it is advisable to drive with only the sidelights on
14dyf2j.why: Sidelights alone are not enough; you need fog lights or dipped headlights.

1dhzdcf.q: In dense fog it is advisable to keep the left turn indicator on
1dhzdcf.why: The indicator signals a turn and must not be left on in fog, because it would confuse other drivers.

1h0kyxf.q: In dense fog it is advisable to drive in a zigzag to make your presence more noticeable
1h0kyxf.why: Zigzagging is dangerous and forbidden; you show your presence with the proper lights.

1ku0vom.q: In thick fog it is advisable to follow the vehicle ahead as closely as possible.
1ku0vom.why: In thick fog visibility is poor, so you must increase the safety distance (distanza di sicurezza), not reduce it.

knqstq.q: In thick fog it is advisable to sound the horn continuously.
knqstq.why: The horn is only for warning of immediate danger. Sounding it continuously is not allowed and does not make you safer.

zivm4.q: In thick fog it is advisable to keep the seat belt unfastened to be readier to leave the vehicle in case of an accident.
zivm4.why: The seat belt (cintura di sicurezza) must always be fastened. It protects you in a crash, especially in poor visibility.

ziqg7b.q: A driver involved in a road accident has the obligation to stop and assist any injured people.
ziqg7b.why: A driver involved in an accident must stop and help any injured people. Failing to do so is a criminal offence (omissione di soccorso).

1kg2etp.q: A driver involved in a road accident must give the injured parties their personal details and the details of the licence, the plate and the vehicle's insurance.
1kg2etp.why: After an accident with damage, drivers must exchange personal details, licence details, plate number and insurance information.

17zosgt.q: A driver involved in a road accident must avoid altering the traces if the dynamics of the accident need to be reconstructed.
17zosgt.why: If the accident has to be reconstructed, evidence on the road must not be altered, except what is needed to help people or clear traffic.

1jwyeqh.q: A driver involved in a road accident may use the pre-printed forms provided by their own insurer to report it to the insurance company.
1jwyeqh.why: The accident can be reported using the pre-printed amicable report form (modulo CAI) supplied by insurers.

3ymn95.q: After a road accident it is mandatory to place the portable warning sign on the rear window of the vehicle before leaving.
3ymn95.why: The warning triangle (segnale mobile di pericolo) is placed on the road behind a stopped vehicle. It is not put on the rear window before driving off.

1b8hb7o.q: After a road accident it is mandatory to cover the vehicle with a plastic sheet.
1b8hb7o.why: No rule requires covering the vehicle. The duties are to help, signal the danger and exchange details.

ke5skh.q: After a road accident it is mandatory, at night only, to place the portable warning sign near the vehicle.
ke5skh.why: The warning triangle is required whenever a stopped vehicle obstructs traffic, by day as well as by night, not only at night.

thjorj.q: After a road accident it is mandatory to immediately place the vehicle on the sidewalk.
thjorj.why: The vehicle should be moved so it does not obstruct traffic if possible, but never onto the sidewalk (marciapiede), which is for pedestrians.

6b67iw.q: After a road accident, it is mandatory to signal the stationary vehicle with the portable warning sign even in built-up areas.
6b67iw.why: According to the official answer, the triangle is not always compulsory in built-up areas; it matters mainly outside them and where visibility is limited.

vvdenl.q: It is advisable for the driver to personally carry out maintenance on the injection pump of their own vehicle.
vvdenl.why: The injection pump is a delicate precision part. Its maintenance should be left to a specialised workshop (officina).

1lp05ck.q: The distance travelled during the reaction time does not vary with speed.
1lp05ck.why: The vehicle keeps moving during reaction time, so the higher the speed, the greater the distance covered.

u0fbkp.q: Correct engine operation is guaranteed by the red lubrication oil warning light staying constantly on.
u0fbkp.why: A red oil warning light that stays on signals insufficient oil pressure. Stop the engine and check it; it is not a sign of normal operation.

1yidc7q.q: It is permitted to improve the performance of your vehicle by increasing the engine displacement.
1yidc7q.why: Changing engine displacement (cilindrata) alters the type-approved specifications. It is only allowed with official approval and an updated registration document.

1ozusqz.q: It is not necessary to adjust unbalanced brakes if the driver is able to correct the vehicle's abnormal behaviour by steering.
1ozusqz.why: Unbalanced brakes must always be adjusted. Correcting them with steering is dangerous and reduces stability when braking.

zy7wa4.q: On a slippery road, to ensure the best grip when braking, it is advisable to press the brake pedal all the way down.
zy7wa4.why: On a slippery road, pressing the brake fully can lock the wheels. Brake gently and progressively instead.

jetiz3.q: It is permitted to increase the performance of your vehicle by modifying the electronic settings of the control unit that manages fuel injection.
jetiz3.why: Modifying the engine control unit (centralina) changes the approved power and emissions figures, and is not allowed without approval.

ecbx5w.q: When a passenger has to get in or out, it is advisable to do so on the sidewalk side or, if there is none, on the side away from traffic.
ecbx5w.why: Passengers should board and exit on the sidewalk (marciapiede) side or, if none, on the side away from traffic, to reduce risk.

1w4th2r.q: When a passenger has to get in or out of the vehicle, the door must be opened only when it does not endanger other road users.
1w4th2r.why: Doors may be opened only when this creates no danger or obstruction for other road users.

9mxam8.q: When a passenger has to get in or out of the vehicle, they must be made to wait until the vehicle has come to a complete stop.
9mxam8.why: Boarding and exiting must happen only when the vehicle is completely stopped, to avoid falls and accidents.

xln94s.q: When a child has to get in or out of the vehicle, it is advisable for an adult to supervise.
xln94s.why: Children do not judge road dangers well, so an adult should supervise them when they get in or out.

1jmvo7u.q: When a passenger has to get out, keep in mind that opening the right-hand door is free of any risk or danger.
1jmvo7u.why: The right-hand door can also be dangerous, for example for cyclists, motorcyclists or pedestrians approaching. Always check first.

1tfsllw.q: If the vehicle is stuck in snow or sand and cannot be moved, it is advisable to put something that gives friction under the slipping wheel (pieces of wood, floor mats, etc.).
1tfsllw.why: Putting rough material under the spinning wheel increases friction and helps the vehicle get moving.

15n4h9f.q: If the vehicle is stuck in snow or sand and cannot start in first gear, it is appropriate to engage a higher gear.
15n4h9f.why: A higher gear reduces torque at the wheels and limits wheel spin, making it easier to get going.

1i493yd.q: On a snow-covered road the vehicle's grip is lower than on an icy road.
1i493yd.why: Ice gives the lowest grip of all. Snow is slippery but offers more grip than ice.

1qk0pm6.q: Rear-end collisions mainly occur because of high speed.
1qk0pm6.why: High speed lengthens braking distances and shortens reaction time, causing many rear-end collisions (tamponamenti).

c8mk2z.q: Rear-end collisions happen more often when the safety distance is not respected.
c8mk2z.why: Without an adequate safety distance there is no room to brake in time when the vehicle ahead slows down.

1nxxw81.q: Rear-end collisions mainly occur because of driver inattention.
1nxxw81.why: Distraction delays reaction and is one of the main causes of rear-end collisions.

9yo3mb.q: Rear-end collisions mainly occur because of a sudden failure of the parking brake.
9yo3mb.why: The parking brake (freno di stazionamento) is not used while driving. The main causes are speed, inattention and insufficient distance.

1ecqpzz.q: Rear-end collisions mainly occur between cars equipped with power steering.
1ecqpzz.why: Power steering (servosterzo) has no link to rear-end collisions, which are mainly caused by speed, inattention and short distance.

1bqw90q.q: When driving through a long tunnel, if long queues of vehicles form, it is advisable to increase the safety distance to prevent flames from spreading quickly in case of fire.
1bqw90q.why: In a tunnel with queues, a larger gap between vehicles limits how fast a fire can spread.

1qfjres.q: When driving through a long tunnel, in case of fire you must leave the vehicle quickly, following the signs to escape routes or to safe places protected by fire doors.
1qfjres.why: In a tunnel fire you leave the vehicle and quickly follow the signs to escape routes or fire-door-protected safe areas.

yl71wg.q: When driving through a long tunnel, in case of fire you must follow the voice instructions of service staff or firefighters, to avoid heading in the wrong direction.
yl71wg.why: Voice instructions from tunnel staff or firefighters point to the correct exit and must be followed.

16xmv77.q: When driving through a long tunnel, in case of fire you must follow the emergency signs, even if they clearly conflict with the voice orders given by firefighters.
16xmv77.why: If they conflict, the instructions of firefighters or staff take priority, since they know the real situation.

2b8jkt.q: Motorcycles, having a small frontal profile, are less visible from a distance.
2b8jkt.why: Motorcycles have a small frontal profile, so other drivers notice them later.

ldhytb.q: Car drivers must in general pay particular attention to two-wheeled motor vehicles, as they are less easily visible.
ldhytb.why: Two-wheeled motor vehicles are harder to see, so car drivers must pay them particular attention.

aro3e9.q: Car drivers, when opening doors, must pay particular attention to two-wheeled motor vehicles, as they are less visible.
aro3e9.why: Before opening a door, check for approaching motorcycles and scooters, which are hard to see and often filtering past.

uc8ys1.q: When crossing junctions you must always consider the possibility that a two-wheeled motor vehicle, which has overtaken the stopped vehicles, may arrive without being visible from a distance.
uc8ys1.why: A motorcycle passing a stopped queue can appear suddenly, so always allow for it at junctions.

nlbjsc.q: In heavy traffic with queued vehicles, before opening the doors to get out of your parked vehicle, you must always consider that a two-wheeled motor vehicle may arrive overtaking the stopped queued vehicles on the right.
nlbjsc.why: In queued traffic, motorcycles may pass between vehicles, so check carefully before opening a door.

4keqcr.q: When overtaking a two-wheeled motor vehicle, especially at high speed, a good lateral safety distance must be kept.
4keqcr.why: When passing a motorcycle, especially a fast one, leave a good side gap so as not to unbalance or hit it.

10oepw3.q: When driving on the road, to be more visible, motorcycles must keep their dipped headlights on even during the day.
10oepw3.why: Motorcycles must always ride with dipped headlights (anabbaglianti) on, even by day, to be more visible.

nqcaew.q: When driving in built-up areas, motorcyclists may in any case use the horn when approaching junctions.
nqcaew.why: In built-up areas the horn is allowed only to warn of immediate danger, not routinely at every junction.

zsqwvq.q: On roads where snow chains are mandatory, in case of snowfall, two-wheeled vehicle drivers are nevertheless allowed to circulate.
zsqwvq.why: Where chains are compulsory, two-wheeled vehicles cannot circulate during snowfall.

12r92vv.q: Motorcycle riders are more easily noticed by other car drivers because they are noisier.
12r92vv.why: Visibility depends on size and position, not noise. Motorcyclists remain harder to notice.

1m5npy1.q: Drivers of two-wheeled vehicles, having a small frontal profile, are more visible from a distance.
1m5npy1.why: A small frontal profile makes two-wheeled vehicles less visible from a distance, not more.

1f1cy2t.q: Drivers of two-wheeled vehicles, being less easily visible from a distance, must in any case ride with their high beams on during night hours.
1f1cy2t.why: At night dipped beams are used. High beams (abbaglianti) are used only outside built-up areas and when they do not dazzle others.

o57h8q.q: A motorcyclist's clothing has no effect on their visibility in traffic.
o57h8q.why: Light, bright or reflective clothing makes a motorcyclist more visible.

16b4u2p.q: Tram rails are a road feature that can be dangerous for the circulation of two-wheeled vehicles.
16b4u2p.why: Tram rails can trap or slip the narrow wheels of two-wheeled vehicles.

140d3z1.q: Pedestrian crossing stripes painted on the carriageway are a road feature that can be dangerous for the circulation of two-wheeled vehicles.
140d3z1.why: The paint of pedestrian crossings (strisce pedonali) can be slippery and dangerous for two-wheeled vehicles.

vdibvz.q: Manholes on the carriageway are a road feature that can be dangerous for the circulation of two-wheeled vehicles.
vdibvz.why: Metal manhole covers (tombini) can be slippery and uneven, and are dangerous for narrow wheels.

1puwzms.q: Tram rails are particularly dangerous for the circulation of two-wheeled vehicles when the road surface is wet.
1puwzms.why: When wet, rails become even more slippery, with a high risk of losing grip.

h990i8.q: Pedestrian crossing stripes painted on the carriageway are particularly dangerous for the circulation of two-wheeled vehicles when the road surface is wet.
h990i8.why: On wet roads the paint of pedestrian crossings greatly reduces the grip of two-wheeled vehicles.

w277xe.q: Manholes on the carriageway are particularly dangerous for the circulation of two-wheeled vehicles when the road surface is wet.
w277xe.why: When wet, metal manhole covers (tombini) become very slippery for two-wheelers.

suytkd.q: When riding a two-wheeled vehicle on a wet road, braking is particularly dangerous if the vehicle's wheels are on tram rails, pedestrian crossing stripes or manholes.
suytkd.why: Braking on wet rails, crossing stripes or manholes can lock the wheels and cause a fall.

150n7l0.q: Passing at speed over manholes or tram rails on a two-wheeled vehicle can cause loss of road holding and steering control, resulting in skids or falls.
150n7l0.why: Crossing these features at speed can cause loss of grip and control, leading to skidding or falling.

p5m0w2.q: Tram rails or manholes on the carriageway do not constitute a danger for a driver of a two-wheeled vehicle.
p5m0w2.why: Rails and manholes are hazardous for two-wheeled vehicles, especially in the wet.

6iwrld.q: When, on a rainy day, you have to cross tram rails or manholes on the carriageway on a two-wheeled vehicle, you must accelerate sharply before crossing them.
6iwrld.why: Slow down before the obstacle and cross it as smoothly as possible, without sharp acceleration or braking.

1c1ygkq.q: When, on a rainy day, you have to cross tram rails or manholes on the carriageway on a two-wheeled vehicle, it is good to stand up on the pedals before crossing them.
1c1ygkq.why: Standing on the pedals does not make the crossing safe. Slow down and cross with the vehicle stable.

1k2jhy3.q: When, on a rainy day, you have to cross tram rails or manholes on the carriageway on a two-wheeled vehicle, it is good to do so in a wheelie so the front steering wheel does not pass over them.
1k2jhy3.why: A wheelie is dangerous and causes loss of control. Slow down and cross carefully instead.

1grmy8g.q: Tram rails or manholes on the carriageway are a danger for a driver of a two-wheeled vehicle only if their vehicle has an automatic gearbox.
1grmy8g.why: The danger comes from reduced wheel grip, not from the type of gearbox.

1j5f34z.q: If you must ride a two-wheeled vehicle on a carriageway shared by vehicles and trams, it is good, if possible, to ride with both wheels in the groove of the tram rail.
1j5f34z.why: Wheels in the rail groove can get trapped, so rails should be crossed and not followed inside the groove.
